title: Boundary-induced geometrical frustration in a square Rydberg-atom lattice
authors: Marco Rigobello, Luka Pavešić, Daniel Jaschke, Pietro Silvi, Marco Di Liberto, Simone Montangero, Simone Notarnicola
abstract: We study geometric defects in square-lattice Rydberg-atom arrays induced by lattice-size parity in the striated density-wave phase. While odd-sized lattices select a single striated domain, even-sized lattices seed incompatible domains at the four corners, resulting in a π/2-rotation invariant state with a geometrical defect emanating from the lattice center. At larger detunings, we instead identify a π-rotation-invariant state with two domains nucleated by opposite corners and separated by a one-dimensional diagonal defect. We probe the state-preparation protocol on the Aquila atomic quantum processor and benchmark it with equilibrium and real-time dynamics tensor-network simulations. Our results assess the role of boundaries and lattice size in determining the global ordering in programmable quantum matter.
summary: This paper explores how the geometry and size of a Rydberg-atom lattice dictate its global quantum order, revealing frustration effects based on lattice parity. By comparing experimental measurements with tensor-network simulations, the authors map out transitions between $C_4$-symmetric and $C_2$-symmetric ordered states. It highlights the crucial role of boundaries in stabilizing specific defect patterns in programmable quantum matter.
main_problem: The study investigates how lattice size parity and boundary conditions induce geometrical frustration and determine the global ordering in programmable quantum matter.
main_result: The system exhibits distinct ordered phases depending on lattice size and detuning, transitioning from a $C_4$-symmetric state to a $C_2$-symmetric state characterized by a diagonal defect.
method: The research combines experimental protocols on the Aquila quantum processor with advanced numerical simulations like DMRG and TDVP using tensor networks.
model_or_system: The system is a square lattice of Rydberg atoms, modeled by an effective spin-1/2 Hamiltonian involving Rydberg excitation number operators and long-range dipole-dipole interactions.
key_observables: Plaquette order parameter ($\Pi_r$), boundary rotational correlator ($\Phi$), and the staggered magnetization proxy ($S(\pi, \pi)$).
important_parameters: Lattice size parity (odd vs. even), detuning ($\Delta$), and interaction strength ($V_{rr'}$).
main_assumptions: The experimental ramp protocol may not reach the highest detuning regimes simulated, and larger simulations might artificially break true $C_4$ symmetry.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the ground state and dynamics across different detuning regimes, contrasting the effects of lattice size parity (odd vs. even) on the resulting global order and defect structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, experimentally relevant platform (Rydberg arrays) to study fundamental concepts of geometric frustration, symmetry breaking, and boundary effects in quantum many-body systems.
